newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey bus crash injured treated by Dutch doctors.
newsitem.headline: Turkey bus crash injured treated by Dutch doctors.

text.p: A group of Dutch doctors arrived in southern Turkey on Friday to treat people injured when a coach carrying German and Dutch holidaymakers plunged down a ravine, killing 11 people.
A Dutch plane was scheduled to land near the popular Mediterranean resort of Antalya late on Friday to take 11 injured Dutch citizens back to Holland, one of the doctors told Reuters.
Ten foreign tourists and one Turk died in Thursday's crash when a coach skidded of the road and plunged 30 metres (100 feet) down a ravine. Twenty-one people were injured.
The bus was carrying around 30 tourists, mostly Dutch and Germans, from Antalya to the inland town of Pamukkale.
Turkey has one of the worst road traffic death rates in the world. Almost 6,000 people lost their lives in traffic accidents last year.
